page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a bundled 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core CPU stress tests, placing the processor in the top 10% of tested hardware. However, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average tier. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 1034.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 117.28 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server demonstrates average capabilities in database operations, redis SET operations, and static web serving. A notable tradeoff is observed in LLM inference workloads; while small 135M model processing is average, prompt processing for medium 7B models drops to the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of dedicated resources, combining a substantial 1920 GB NVMe SSD with a memory-optimized 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This makes it a balanced option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU execution without the premium of specialized memory-only instances. The server is well-suited for database hosting, memory-intensive web serving, caching layers like Redis, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from local NVMe storage and dedicated AMD EPYC processing.
